current_title: Sr VP Allison Office of Corporate Affairs & Sr VP Allison Transmission Marketing, Sales and Service
message_1:
John, with Dana Incorporated now part of Allison Transmission, the catalogs are the next thing that has to look like one company.
Two or three catalogs created by different studios in different years rarely line up after a deal, and re-shooting or re-rendering a full product library is not usually in an integration budget, so the hero products get redone and the rest carries the old look for a couple of years.
Where imagery is generated from CAD instead, the branding is a parameter, so it applies across the library at once rather than product by product.
message_2: Is the imagery refresh inside the integration scope, or a separate project after it?
message_3:
That split is where most of these end up stretching.
I’m with VNTANA. I recorded three minutes going through your product pages, what still carries the old identity and what the same pages look like once the imagery is generated from CAD. No pitch in it, and it forwards well if you need to show someone: {{video_link}}
when_they_say_yes: Here it is: {{video_link}}. Three minutes, and the second half is the part worth watching. If you want to go through it properly: {{meeting_link}}

Tim, with TC Transcontinental Packaging now part of ProAmpac, the catalogs are the next thing that has to look like one company.
Two or three catalogs created by different studios in different years rarely line up after a deal, and re-shooting or re-rendering a full product library is not usually in an integration budget, so the hero products get redone and the rest carries the old look for a couple of years.
Where imagery is generated from CAD instead, the branding is a parameter, so it applies across the library at once rather than product by product.
message_2: Is the imagery refresh inside the integration scope, or a separate project after it?
message_3:
That split is where most of these end up stretching.
I’m with VNTANA. I recorded three minutes going through your product pages, what still carries the old identity and what the same pages look like once the imagery is generated from CAD. No pitch in it, and it forwards well if you need to show someone: {{video_link}}
when_they_say_yes: Here it is: {{video_link}}. Three minutes, and the second half is the part worth watching. If you want to go through it properly: {{meeting_link}}

Two or three catalogs created by different studios in different years rarely line up after a deal, and re-shooting or re-rendering a full product library is not usually in an integration budget, so the hero products get redone and the rest carries the old look for a couple of years.
Where imagery is generated from CAD instead, the branding is a parameter, so it applies across the library at once rather than product by product.
message_2: Is the imagery refresh inside the integration scope, or a separate project after it?
message_3:
That split is where most of these end up stretching.
I’m with VNTANA. I recorded three minutes going through your product pages, what still carries the old identity and what the same pages look like once the imagery is generated from CAD. No pitch in it, and it forwards well if you need to show someone: {{video_link}}
when_they_say_yes: Here it is: {{video_link}}. Three minutes, and the second half is the part worth watching. If you want to go through it properly: {{meeting_link}}
